title: Five years of submissions to Science and Science Advances: Vermont Complex Systems looks behind-the-scenes
subtitle: What happens when a paper is submitted to Science? VCSI core faculty Sam Zhang opens the black box

boxSteps.value: The editorial process at elite journals typically operates like a black box — papers go in, decisions come out, but quantitative data about what happens inside is largely hidden from view.

VCSI faculty collaborated with the American Association for the Advancement of Science to open the box — and allow the entire scientific community to trace what happens to every paper submitted to Science and Science Advances.

Between 2015 and 2019, there were **68,047 manuscripts** submitted to science. Each square represents one paper. By the time they go through the review process, **only 6% are accepted to the journal**.

steps.value: **68,047 papers** were submitted to *Science* between 2010 and 2019. Each square represents a paper flowing through the review pipeline.
Every submission first enters the **Board of Reviewing Editors** — a brief editorial review. About 30% (20,755) are rejected here without further review.
Papers that clear the Board of Reviewing Editors (BoRE) may be sent to **peer review**. Only 1 in 4 BoRE-approved papers (11,845) reaches this stage — the rest are rejected by editors.
Of papers reaching peer review, **4,181 are accepted** — just 6% of all submissions. The other 7,664 are rejected after review.
